headline: Somatic variant detection methods are being tested on pangenome, plant and mtDNA data
label: Somatic Variant Detection Methods
summary: Recent preprints and a publication benchmark somatic variant and mobile element calling across pangenome, plant, and human tissue datasets.
synthesis: The common thread is improving how variants are detected and reported from bulk and population sequencing by changing either the reference or the analytical model. A pangenome reference is tested against hg38 for somatic calling in a pediatric AML case, with fewer false-positive indels reported. In barley, composited genomes built from short-read draft strategies are compared for MOA-seq transcription factor footprint analysis across cultivars. mito-overview integrates mtDNA coverage, allele fractions, annotations and long-read co-occurrence into reports, while UMR-seq recovers genetic variants alongside unmethylated regions in a single assay. What is new here is explicit modeling of tissue composition: vafSOMA assigns cell layers to somatic mutations in plant bulk data, and the multi-platform retrotransposition framework benchmarks long-read and MEI-targeted methods in human tissues.
